This is regulation by pulse width modulation!
Q1 changes the pulse width of its output which changes the filter's average output voltage, compensating for any load changes.
In other words, any increase in the load will try to lower the output voltage, which will increase the pulse width, bringing the voltage back up.
With Q1 ON more of the time, the output voltage through the filter is raised.
If the filtered DC voltage is less than the reference voltage, Q1 is ON more than it is OFF.
With Q1 OFF more of the time, the output voltage through the filter is lowered.
If the filtered DC voltage is the same or larger than the reference voltage, Q1 is turned OFF more than it is turned ON.

In other words, the regulator operates using pulse width, this is where the name pulse width modulated regulator or power supply comes from.
If Q1's output pulses are wide, the filtered DC voltage is HIGH, or the average voltage of the pulses produce a higher voltage.
